bugs.summary: sync with upstream TRE + apply R patches
bugs.creator: kevinushey

comments.text:
## Summary

Updates the bundled TRE from its 2009 base to current upstream, which has absorbed most of R's local patches; pending upstream PRs restore the rest. Also includes fixes for a couple other issues caught along the way: wrong back-reference matches (PR#17259) and multi-gigabyte allocations when compiling short patterns with nested bounds.

## Details

The sources come from the `r-integration` branch of https://github.com/kevinushey/tre, my fork of upstream TRE (https://github.com/laurikari/tre), at commit 512d52fcef. The branch starts from upstream master at commit 71bfcaf0af39 (2026-05-23, still its head) and merges those PRs. R's own changes are confined to three files. `src/extra/tre/R_changes` lists the PRs and the visible changes, mainly in bound parsing (`a{300,}` is now an error). Upstream PRs 131 and 167 supersede the PR#18995 patch.

Reproducible example: attached as `tre-upstream-sync-repro.R`; it fails before the patch and passes after.

Proposed patches, both against r90915:

- `tre-upstream-sync.diff` replaces `src/extra/tre` (no Makefile changes) and adds cases to `tests/reg-fuzz.R`. `make check` passes on macOS, `reg-fuzz.R` also under ASan, and CI passes on Linux and Windows.
- `regex-unwind-leaks.diff` (independent) stops `grep()`, `gsub()`, `regexpr()`, `regexec()` and `strsplit()` leaking the compiled pattern and translation buffers when an error or `options(warn = 2)` unwinds them.

Also submitted as https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/pull/302 and https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/pull/400, where CI results can be seen. Related: PR#17766.

comments.text:
Note that one of the remaining STF milestones has "Re-enable upstream sync from embedded legacy code" also for TRE.  

Now that this is actively maintained again it would be good to look into using
a system TRE by default (if available), and perhaps add a configure option like

  --with-internal-tre 
  --with-internal-TRE

(not sure which one is better) for controlling this.

Patches welcome ...

comments.creator: kevinushey
comments.text:
It looks like R already has `--with-system-tre` (off by default), which seems like the natural switch (or would you prefer to change that flag?)

The challenge is upstream: I've proposed the fixes R needs there (https://github.com/laurikari/tre/pulls?q=is%3Apr+author%3Akevinushey, plus #131 and #142 by the upstream maintainers), but none have been merged yet. The only release is still 0.9.0 from 2024, which is what Debian, Fedora and Homebrew ship. Building R against it today would undo fixes R already has; for example, the PR#18995 patterns read past the pattern buffer again under ASan.

In the meantime, the attached patch covers the upstream-sync part of the milestone: the bundled copy becomes upstream master plus those PRs, with R's own changes confined to three files, so later syncs are a straight copy.

comments.text:
Created attachment 4168
patch: keep an assertion required under a bare quantifier, e.g. "^*$" (apply after re-applying r90973)

Thanks, Kurt. `.onLoad()` in R.devices runs `devOptions("*")`, which greps `"^*$"` against the known device types, `"*"` included. The 0.8.0 copy read `^*` as a required `^`, so nothing matched; the new copy (laurikari/tre#163) reads it as zero or more `^`, so every type matches and `devOptions()` recurses on `"*"` forever.

POSIX leaves `^*` undefined, and glibc and PCRE reject it, so R.devices relies on undefined behaviour. The attached patch, to apply after re-applying r90973, restores the 0.8.0 meaning for such bare assertions only and keeps upstream's fix for `(^)*`. With it, R.devices installs and `make check` passes; a regression test is included.

I've also sent Henrik a small R.devices fix that matches exact type names first: https://github.com/HenrikBengtsson/R.devices/pull/44. Happy to look at anything else your r90980 run turns up.
comments.creator: kevinushey
kevinushey
comments.text:
Sorry, I misspoke earlier -- in my last comment I attributed the change in `^*$` to the TRE update. TRE 0.9.0 and upstream `master` both match `^*$` only against the empty string, just as R 4.6 does. The change that broke R.devices comes from the still-open [laurikari/tre#163](https://github.com/laurikari/tre/pull/163).

We included #163 in our integration branch because it fixes a longstanding matching bug reported in [PR#17992](https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=17992). For example, `(^|\b)a` misses the `a` in `"this is a word"`, but reversing the alternatives to `(\b|^)a` finds it. Both patterns should match at that word boundary.

Let me know if you'd prefer to take #163 plus the add-on patch, or if you'd prefer the TRE sync without #163.

(In reply to Kevin Ushey from comment #13)
> Let me know if you'd prefer to take #163 plus the add-on patch, or if you'd
> prefer the TRE sync without #163.

I'd expect less trouble by omitting the unsettled TRE PR#163 for now, so postponing the fix for Bug 17992.

comments.text:
Thanks.  I can confirm that with the two patches R.devices still works.

However, the patches do not apply clearly for tests/reg-fuzz.R from r91001: could you please generate one combined patch which can be applied without changes?

Also, applying the patches makes emayili fail its checks with

> compliant("alice@example.com")
Warning in grepl(".{256,}", domain) :
  TRE pattern compilation error 'Maximum repetition in {} larger than 255'
Error in grepl(".{256,}", domain) : 
  invalid regular expression '.{256,}', reason 'Maximum repetition in {} larger than 255'

I see that

./src/extra/tre/R_changes: - {n,} with n > RE_DUP_MAX (255) is now rejected with REG_BADMAX.  The

so this is "as intended"?
comments.creator: Kurt.Hornik

comments.text:
Right, that one is intended: it is the behaviour of the released TRE 0.9.0 (laurikari/tre@32f4cfd), not of one of the pending pull requests. The 0.8.0 copy checked only the maximum, so .{256,} was accepted while .{256,300} was already an error. POSIX only guarantees RE_DUP_MAX = 255.

I can prepare a patch for emayili, and I'll also prepare a unified patch shortly.
comments.creator: kevinushey

comments.text:
Created attachment 4189
patch: update src/extra/tre to upstream TRE plus pending PRs, without #163 (against r91002)

I've attached the combined patch, against r91002. It replaces attachment 4141 and attachment 4171, and re-enables the `tests/reg-fuzz.R` block that r90987 commented out.

Beyond those two patches, it documents the 255 limit in `?regex`, notes in `R_changes` that the stricter check is part of the TRE 0.9.0 release, and adds a regression test. The POSIX wording is in [XBD 9.4.6](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/basedefs/V1_chap09.html#tag_09_04_06) and [`<limits.h>`](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/basedefs/limits.h.html).

The emayili fix is at https://github.com/datawookie/emayili/pull/169; the result of that `grepl()` was never used, so it now calls `nchar()` instead.

If you would rather keep such patterns working until emayili is updated, the limit is the single definition `#define RE_DUP_MAX 255` in `src/extra/tre/tre.h`; the check in `tre-parse.c` and the error message both follow it. Any larger decimal value makes `.{256,}` compile again, and memory stays bounded by `TRE_MAX_POS`. The `?regex` paragraph and the `reg-fuzz.R` test in this patch state 255, so they would need the new value too. I'm happy to send that variant if you prefer it.
